claims.text: Substituting Al for Mn in CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys promotes formation of a thermodynamically stable protective oxide above 900 °C.
Substituting Al for Mn promotes formation of a coherent protective oxide above 900 °C.
Al has lower oxygen diffusivity than Mn in the relevant alloy or oxide system.
Al has an oxidation enthalpy favorable for forming a protective oxide.
Al drives formation of a mixed alumina/Cr-oxide film.
The mixed alumina/Cr-oxide film accommodates thermal strain better than the oxide formed on the Mn-containing alloy.
Mn has higher mobility than Al under the stated oxidation conditions.
Higher Mn mobility produces volatile and discontinuous oxides.
The Mn-rich oxides are prone to cracking and spallation.
Selective oxidation is governed by elemental diffusion kinetics and thermodynamic oxidation potentials.
Al's low diffusivity and strong oxygen affinity facilitate growth of a coherent, slow-growing oxide.
Oxide phase continuity enables stress relief.
Rapid oxidation associated with high Mn diffusivity produces volatile products that crack and spall.
Under identical conditions, Al-containing HEAs will have a more continuous and adherent oxide layer than Mn-containing HEAs.
Al-containing HEAs will exhibit lower oxide-scale residual stresses than Mn-containing HEAs.
Al-containing HEAs will exhibit less oxide cracking and spallation than Mn-containing HEAs.
The proposed comparison is applicable to single-phase, homogenized CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive environments.
An identically processed Mn-containing alloy serves as the controlled baseline for the Al-containing alloy.

contradictions.description: The stated domain is strictly above 900 °C, but the example exposure range is 900–1000 °C and therefore includes 900 °C.
